# About the society
:::
:::

::: {.prose}

The Computational Social Science Society is a research and learning community at
Boğaziçi University, led by [Assoc. Prof. Başak Taraktaş](https://basaktaraktas.com)
in the Department of Political Science and International Relations. It brings together
undergraduate and graduate students, alongside faculty, who work on social questions
using computational methods.

## What the society is for

Computational social science sits between disciplines, which means it is rarely
anyone's home department. A student in sociology who wants to learn network analysis,
or one in computer engineering who wants to ask a substantive social question, often
has nowhere obvious to go. The society exists to be that place: a standing group where
methods are taught horizontally, between peers, rather than only vertically through
coursework.

## How sessions work

We meet weekly during term. A typical session has one of three shapes:

**Hands-on workshop.** A member walks the group through a method with real data —
fitting an ERGM, scraping a corpus, building a model in NetLogo. Everyone codes along.

**Paper discussion.** We read a recent methods or applications paper and work through
what it actually did, including the parts the abstract glosses over.

**Project session.** Members present work in progress and get feedback. Several of the
projects on our [projects page](projects.qmd) started this way.

## Who can join

Anyone at Boğaziçi. There is no application and no prerequisite. Some members arrive
already writing Python; others have never opened a terminal. Both are useful to have in
the room, and the second group is why the workshops exist.

## Language

Sessions run in Turkish and English depending on who is present. Materials are usually
in English, since that is where the literature is, but nobody is expected to present in
a language they are uncomfortable with.

:::
